## Sign in

Go to [colab.research.google.com](https://colab.research.google.com) and sign in
with your **WFU Google account** (`yourname@wfu.edu`).

Click **New notebook**. 

## Your first cell

Click a cell, type, and press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}} to run it.

```{python}
2 + 2
```

The output appears underneath. Press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}} again and the next
cell runs.

## Loading course data

Every data set we use lives on this website. 

```{python}
import pandas as pd

DATA = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LucyMcGowan/sta-363-f26/main/data/"
Auto = pd.read_csv(DATA + "Auto.csv")
Auto.head()
```

That `DATA` line appears at the top of every exercise. Copy it once and change
only the file name. The full list is on the [Course Data](data.qmd) page.

## What is already installed

| Package | What we use it for |
|---|---|
| `pandas` | data frames |
| `numpy` | arrays and simulation |
| `matplotlib` | figures |
| `scikit-learn` | every model until Thanksgiving |
| `torch` | neural networks, already installed |


## The one install

When we get to neural networks we may need a few additional packages. PyTorch itself is already on Colab, but three helper packages are not. Put this cell at the top of the
notebook and run it once per session:

```{python}
#| eval: false
%pip install -q pytorch-lightning torchinfo torchmetrics
```


## Turning on the GPU

We will not often need to use GPUs. If we do, go to
**Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Change runtime type** and pick a **GPU**
accelerator. Check that it worked:

```{python}
#| eval: false
import torch
torch.cuda.is_available()
```

`True` means you have one. `False` means Colab did not allocate one right now,
which happens on the free tier. Everything we do will run without a GPU, just
more slowly.

## Saving your work

A Colab notebook you open from a link is read only until you save your own copy.

**File** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Save a copy in Drive**

Do this at the start of every class. Your copy lives in a Colab Notebooks folder
in your WFU Google Drive and saves automatically after that.

## Problem sets

Each problem set is a notebook. Open it from the {{< fa file-lines >}} icon on
the [Schedule](schedule.qmd), which lands you in Colab on a read only copy.

1. **File** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Save a copy in Drive**, then work in your copy.  
2. Run the setup cell at the top before anything else.  
3. Type prose into the cells that read *Type your answer here*. Double click the cell to edit it, then press {{< kbd Shift-Enter >}} to render it.  
4. Type code into the blank code cells.  
5. Before you turn it in, use **Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Restart session and run all** and check that everything still runs.  

To submit, click **Share** in the top right, set **General access** to *Anyone
with the link*, click **Copy link**, and paste that link into Canvas. If the
link is set to *Restricted* I cannot open it, so check that before you submit.

## Things to keep in mind

**The runtime disconnects.** If you leave a notebook idle, it may disconnect. If this happens just re-run your cells from the top. 

**Cells remember what you ran, not what is on screen.** If you delete a cell that defined `X`, `X` still exists until the runtime restarts. If you are having trouble debugging, sometimes this is the underlying reason. Use **Runtime** {{< fa arrow-right >}} **Restart session and
run all**.

**Order matters, not position.** Running cells out of order will work and is a
common cause of confusing errors. See [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.qmd).

## Working locally instead

Everything we learn will work the same way locally. However, I can help with Colab problems in class; local installation problems are better suited to office hours.
